initial_1.title: Enhanced Markdown Specification
initial_1.text:
### Notion-flavored Markdown Notion-flavored Markdown is a variant of standard Markdown with additional features to support all Block and Rich text types. Use tabs for indentation. Use backslashes to escape characters. For example, \* will render as * and not as a bold delimiter. These are the characters that should be escaped: \ * ~ ` $ [ ] < > { } | ^ Block types: Markdown blocks use a {color="Color"} attribute list to set a block color. Text: Rich text {color="Color"} Children Headings: # Rich text {color="Color"} ## Rich text {color="Color"} ### Rich text {color="Color"} #### Rich text {color="Color"} (Headings 5 and 6 are not supported in Notion and will be converted to heading 4.) Bulleted list: - Rich text {color="Color"} Children Numbered list: 1. Rich text {color="Color"} Children Bulleted and numbered list items should contain inline rich text -- otherwise they will render as empty list items, which look awkward in the Notion UI. (The inline text should be rich text -- any other block type will not be rendered inline, but as a child to an empty list item.) Empty line: Notion renders blocks with appropriate spacing, so there is almost never a need to use empty lines. To render correctly as an empty line, must be on its own line with no other text. Empty lines without will be stripped out. Rich text types: Bold: **Rich text** Italic: *Rich text* Strikethrough: ~~Rich text~~ Underline: Rich text Inline code: `Code` Multi-line inline code: `Line 1
Line 2
Line 3` Unlike in standard markdown, never use ordinary newlines inside inline code -- this will break the code span and render backticks as literal text: `Line 1 Line 2` <-- BAD: newline breaks the inline code Link: [Link text](URL) Citation: [^URL] To create a citation, you can either reference a compressed URL like this,[^{{1}}] or a full URL like this.[^example.com] Inline colors: Rich text Inline math: $`Equation`$ The equation must be enclosed in backticks. Inline line breaks within a block (this is mostly useful in multi-line quote blocks, where an ordinary newline character should not be used since it will break up the block structure):
Quote: > Rich text {color="Color"} Children Multi-line quote: > Line 1
Line 2
Line 3 {color="Color"} Unlike in standard markdown, never use ordinary newlines anywhere mid-quote -- this will render as multiple separate quote blocks, not a single multi-line quote: > This is a quote > This is a different, unrelated quote > This is a third quote Use of a single > on a line without any other text should be avoided -- this will render as an empty blockquote, which is not visually appealing. To-do: - [ ] Rich text {color="Color"} Children - [x] Rich text {color="Color"} Children Divider: --- Table:
Data cell Data cell
Data cell Data cell
Note: All table attributes are optional. If omitted, they default to "false". Table structure: - : Root element with optional attributes: - fit-page-width: Whether the table should fill the page width - header-row: Whether the first row is a header - header-column: Whether the first column is a header - : Optional element defining column-wide styles. Do not include a element if you do not want to set any column colors or widths. - : Column definition with optional attributes: - color: The color of the column - width: The width of the column. Leave empty to auto-size. - : Table row with optional color attribute - ) 3. Column color () Contents of table cells: - Table cells can only contain rich text. Other block types (headings, lists, images, etc.) are not supported. - Never use raw HTML formatting tags inside table cells; use the equivalent Notion-flavored Markdown instead, for example **bold** instead of or . Cell merging: - Notion supports merging rectangular groups of cells into a single cell. - You cannot create or modify cell merges through this format. If the user asks you to merge cells, tell them Notion supports it but they must do it in the UI: select the cells, right-click, and choose "Merge cells". To unmerge, use "Unmerge cells" from the same menu. Equation: $$ Equation $$ Code: ```language Code ``` Note: Set the language if known (e.g. mermaid). Do NOT escape special characters inside code blocks. Code block content is literal - write it exactly as it should appear. For example, write `const arr = [1, 2, 3]` NOT `const arr = \[1, 2, 3\]`. Backslash escaping rules only apply outside of code blocks. Mermaid diagrams: Use ```mermaid as the language. Enclose node text in double quotes when it contains special characters like parentheses, e.g. `A["Notion (App + API)"]`. Use `
` for line breaks inside node labels, not \n. Do not use \( or \) inside Mermaid — instead just wrap the whole label in double quotes. XML blocks use the 'color' attribute to set a block color. Mentions: Users, pages, databases, data sources, agents, dates, and datetimes can be mentioned: User name Page title Database name Data source name Agent name The URL must always be provided, and refer to an existing user, page, database, data source, agent, date, or datetime. A user URL has the form user://. The inner text (name/title) is optional. The UI always displays the resolved name. So an alternative self-closing format is also supported: Mentions are clickable and link to the entity. For dates and datetimes, omit the 'end' attribute to mention a single date or datetime. startTime requires timeZone; without timeZone the time is dropped. A datetime range needs all five attributes: start, startTime, end, endTime, and timeZone. is an inline reference only. Do NOT use it to replace a block — removing a block deletes the child page. Colors: Text colors (colored text with transparent background): gray, brown, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple, pink, red Background colors (colored background with contrasting text): gray_bg, brown_bg, orange_bg, yellow_bg, green_bg, blue_bg, purple_bg, pink_bg, red_bg Usage: - Block colors: Add color="Color" to the first line of any block - Inline rich text colors (text colors and background colors are both supported): Use Rich text #### Advanced Block types for Page content The following block types may only be used in page content, not in the chat UI. Toggle:
Rich text Children
Toggle headings use the {toggle="true"} attribute on a heading: Toggle heading 1: # Rich text {toggle="true" color?="Color"} Children Toggle heading 2: ## Rich text {toggle="true" color?="Color"} Children Toggle heading 3: ### Rich text {toggle="true" color?="Color"} Children For toggles and toggle headings, the children must be indented in order for them to be toggleable. If you do not indent the children, they will not be contained within the toggle or toggle heading. Callout: Rich text Children Callouts can contain multiple blocks and nested children, not just inline rich text. Each child block should be indented. For any formatting inside of callout blocks, use Notion-flavored Markdown, not HTML. For instance, bold text in a callout should be wrapped in **, not . Columns: Children Children - ratio: Optional column width as a percentage of the full width, e.g. 50 for half. Omit it to use the default even split when creating columns. When updating existing columns, set every ratio explicitly. Tabs: Tab title Children Each must have its title as the first indented line. The optional icon attribute accepts an emoji or Notion Icon, such as icon="icons/document_gray". Custom emoji: :emoji_name: Page: Title IMPORTANT: A tag represents a subpage (child page) on the current page. WARNING: Using with an existing page URL will MOVE that page into this page as a subpage. Removing that tag from the content will REMOVE that child page from the current page. If moving is not intended use the block instead. Folder: Title A tag represents an existing folder. Use the URL with loadFolder (or fetch in MCP) to read the folder's immediate children, then follow nested URLs to continue traversing. Preserve existing folder tags unless intentionally moving or deleting the folder. Folders cannot be created from Markdown. Database: Title Provide either url or data-source-url attribute: - If 'url' is an existing database URL, including it here will MOVE that database into the current page. If you just want to mention an existing database, use instead. - If 'data-source-url' is an existing data source URL, creates a linked database view. The 'inline' attribute toggles how the database is displayed in the UI. If set to "true", the database is fully visible and interactive on the page. If set to "false", the database is displayed as a sub-page. If you try to set inline to an invalid value, it will default to "false". The 'wiki' attribute indicates whether this database is a wiki. Wiki databases have wiki="true". When creating pages in a wiki database, you MUST use parent type "page" with the wiki's page URL instead of parent type "dataSource". Wiki pages must be created under the database page, not the data source directly. There is no 'Data Source' block type. Data Sources are always inside a Database, and only Databases can be inserted into a Page. Audio: File: Caption Embed (renders an HTML attachment file inline in a sandboxed iframe): Caption "HTML", "HTML block", "HTML artifact", and "HTML embed" all mean an HTML attachment rendered with . Never create one as a code block or file block. Always use for HTML attachment files For files created by the MCP create-attachment tool, use its returned file-upload:// source as the src value. The source is resolved and attached when create-pages or update-page saves the block. Keep the returned file upload ID if you need to retrieve the text later with download-attachment. For files uploaded through the MCP create-file-upload flow, use the upload response's suggested_markdown directly in create-pages or update-page content. To attach the upload to a comment, include suggested_markdown on a separate line in create-comment markdown; comments support up to three file attachments. Image: ![Caption](URL) {color?="Color"} PDF: Caption Video: (Note that source URLs can either be compressed URLs, such as src="{{1}}", or full URLs, such as src="example.com". Full URLs enclosed in curly brackets, like src="{{https://example.com}}" or src="{{example.com}}", do not work.) Table of contents: Synced block: The original source for a synced block. When creating a new synced block, do not provide the URL. After inserting the synced block into a page, the URL will be provided. Children Note: When creating new synced blocks, omit the url attribute - it will be auto-generated. When reading existing synced blocks, the url attribute will be present. Synced block reference: A reference to a synced block. The synced block must already exist and url must be provided. You can directly update the children of the synced block reference and it will update both the original synced block and the synced block reference. If content is unavailable due to permissions, a non-editable notice may be included via the optional notice attribute. Children Meeting notes: Rich text (meeting title) AI-generated summary of the notes + transcript User notes Transcript of the audio (cannot be edited) - The tag contains a raw transcript and cannot be edited by AI, but it can be edited by a user. - When creating new meeting notes blocks, you must omit the and tags. - Only include in a new meeting notes block if the user is SPECIFICALLY requesting note content. - Attempting to include or edit will result in an error. - All content within , , and tags must be indented at least one level deeper than the tag. Custom blocks: Omit url when creating a new instance. Readback adds its instance URL; preserve that URL when editing, reordering, or moving an existing instance. Place the self-closing tag on its own line. It references a saved definition in the destination workspace and inherits its bindings; it does not contain rendered content or instance binding overrides. New placements and definition changes require a live definition readable by the caller. Retaining the same existing instance and definition does not require fresh definition access, even if the definition was deleted. Adding another instance still requires authorization. Public API and MCP requests reject definition-key, which is reserved for App deployments. Reading or placing an existing definition through Markdown does not require separate workspace enablement; definition creation remains in private alpha. Unknown (a block type that is not supported in the API yet):

기록 기준: <mention-date start="2026-10-13" end="2026-10-19"/> · 현재까지 확인한 <mention-date start="2026-10-13"/> 결과. 이번 주 진행 중 보고이며 이후 날짜 작업은 미작성.
### 이번 주 목표
- 기존 GAS/Ability 구조를 유지하면서 정면 피격·천/Hair 물리·회복 VFX의 품질을 개선한다.
- 원작 metadata·Main 실제 검증과 진행 중 거대형 VFX의 상태를 분리한다.
### 현재까지 진행
#### 전투 / GAS / Ability·Event·Tag
- StrongCombo 3타의 6 hit window에 인간형4종 정면 반응을 지정했다. 확정 피해 Event→기존 HitReaction Ability/Task와 자기 실행 cleanup을 재사용했다.
- ASC는 선택 Spec의 입력·held command, Guard/Dodge hit 중재와 태그를 관리한다. 실행 수명은 Action/Combo/Player Ability에 두고 자원은 AttributeSet/GameplayEffect가 소유한다.
- 현재 누적 범위는 기본/차지·연타 콤보, 초록 debug 공격 판정·HP/ST 피해, 회피·Guard/패링·Heal·브루탈, 피격/사망, LockOn과 보간 HUD다.
#### 물리 / 알파 / 환경
- 몬스터 메시35/PhysicsAsset35, RigidBody post-process20·중검 CopyPose와 보조 뼈317개의 천/Hair 반응을 Main에 적용했다. 몸 proxy 접촉과 과한 회전을 줄이고 기존 Player 물리 설정을 재사용했다.
- VFX 카드의 실제 density/Alpha 경로를 교정하고 HeinMach 눈 수를 소폭 줄였다. 원작 색과 gameplay·particle binary 설정을 보존했다.
#### 회복 VFX
- 원작 Recovery의 5종 효과 역할·타이밍과 mesh/texture/LUT를 기존 Heal notify에 연결했다. 손·팔 붉은 에너지·링·입자와 부드러운 알파를 구현했다.
- 기존 Action feedback receipt가 시작/종료·취소·반복 실행의 자원을 정리한다. 새 runtime class/manager/tag는 추가하지 않았다.
### 검증
- StrongCombo Main build/saved·12case/24hit 및 기존 Player 충돌16 회귀 통과.
- 몬스터6종 이동→방향 전환→공격→피격→회복의 보조 물리/finite/body contact와 Player 충돌 회귀 통과.
- Alpha Main saved·실제 shader/RHI·HeinMach 프레임 확인.
- Heal Main build·saved audit·실제 Heal/PlayerAttackCollision 2검사 Success. 효과11 child의 부착·finite, HP/무기/이동, 반복/취소/UnPossess cleanup을 확인했다.
### 미완료 및 리스크
- 사운드 cue/wave·notify·HeinMach 환경음은 Main 저장 기록이 있다. audio-array binding37 수정본은 준비본 검증 후 Main 적용/최종 회귀 대기다. `Saved/ImportReports/GameplayAudio_20261011/ResumeState05.json` 상태를 기준으로 한다.
- Yetuga/Apes 추가 VFX 폴리싱은 Main 선택 반영 후 canonical build·saved 보존·전체 RHI/GAS 패턴·공격 판정 최종 확인 대기다. 완료한 10/11 기본 VFX와 구분한다.
- 참고사진의 분홍/보라 광막은 패링, 백색 중심/붉은 선은 공격으로 재분류했다. 10/13은 분석 기록이며 큰 패링 광막의 새 구현은 아직 없다.
- 방패병 제외 대상 모션 식별, 원작 전용 Niagara/Widget/shader·전체 픽셀/skin/light 동일성, 전 레벨 연속 카메라·Shipping 검증은 미확인이다. Heal 재구성과 보조 물리/알파 TEMP를 원작 직접값으로 표현하지 않는다.
### 다음 계획
1. GiantVFX Main 저장/재생·GAS8 패턴/SkillObject·Player 충돌 회귀와 전달 SHA를 확인한다.
2. 정확한 참고자료에 맞춰 패링 광막·접점과 방패병 어색한 공격을 표적 보완한다.
3. HeinMach/StormPass 실제 연속 전투에서 HUD·카메라·천 접촉·효과 경계를 검수하고 결과를 누적한다.
